claims.text: The ball-milled Mg-Al-Ti-V-Fe-Co powder is a BCC solid solution.
High-energy ball milling produces a nanocrystalline, high-grain-boundary-density powder.
Oxygen is introduced into the powder during milling as dissolved oxygen or surface oxides.
SPS at 900–1000 °C precipitates a continuous nanocrystalline Ti-rich oxide, specifically TiO2, network at BCC grain boundaries.
SPS at 900–1000 °C may precipitate an ordered Ti-Al intermetallic network at BCC grain boundaries.
At 900–1000 °C, the high grain-boundary density activates short-circuit diffusion.
Grain-boundary diffusion drives Ti and milling-derived oxygen segregation and formation of a continuous oxide or intermetallic network.
The grain-boundary network acts as a diffusion barrier to Mg and suppresses Mg volatility.
The grain-boundary network acts as a barrier to oxygen ingress and improves oxidation resistance.
The Ti-rich network forms a self-healing passive film.
The secondary-phase network exerts Zener pinning and prevents excessive grain growth.
Fine grains and secondary-phase precipitation increase alloy hardness.
Grain-boundary pinning by the secondary-phase network enhances densification.
SPS in the proposed temperature window produces a fully dense bulk alloy with a fine-grained BCC matrix.
The proposed microstructure has superior oxidation and corrosion resistance relative to material sintered below 800 °C or above 1000 °C.
Sintering below 800 °C provides insufficient diffusion and densification for bulk formation.
Sintering above 1000 °C causes significant Mg loss, composition deviation, porosity, and microstructural degradation.
The barrier-formation mechanism fails below a critical initial oxygen concentration because the secondary phase cannot nucleate.
A 5–10 minute SPS hold is suitable for producing the proposed microstructure.
An applied SPS pressure of 30–50 MPa is suitable for producing the proposed microstructure.

contradictions.description: The 900–1000 °C interval is described as being below a 1000 °C Mg-volatility threshold even though the interval includes 1000 °C; elsewhere failure is assigned only to temperatures exceeding 1000 °C.
The stated design prepares 950 °C and 1050 °C samples, but the falsification rule requires comparison of the 950 °C sample with an 800 °C sample that is not included in the stated synthesis design.
